terra.problem: The sprinkles punchline compares the earth shining with God's glory to a bakery mishap, making the holy moment part of the joke.
The passage says the glory fills the temple, not that the walls later shine with it.
The chocolate-chip joke compares a reverent response to God's glory with a comic dive, making the holy moment part of the joke.
The text says Ezekiel fell facedown. It does not say he did not turn away or that he stayed in the same spot.
The text does not say Ezekiel was standing in the inner court or that he went up stairs without help.
The claim that angels appear throughout the Bible goes beyond this passage and needs a Scripture reference.
The voice speaks from inside the temple, but the passage does not say the promise is spoken from the throne.
Saying the text puts shame first and the design afterward overlooks the instruction to describe the temple and have the people measure its plan before the conditional instruction in verse 11.
The passage calls all the temple's surrounding territory on top of the mountain most holy; it does not explicitly say the whole mountaintop is covered.
The law's content is stated once. The verse repeats that it is the law of the temple, not the content of the law.
